entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Joachim Vadian, born as Joachim von Watt, was a humanist, scholar, mayor and reformer in the free city of St. Gallen.

As a prominent figure in the Renaissance, Vadian played a crucial role in the development of the St. Gallen Reformation, which sought to modernize the city's governance and religious practices.

His efforts led to the establishment of the St. Gallen City Council, a groundbreaking example of citizen participation in governance.

Vadian's legacy extends beyond his own city, influencing the rise of humanism and civic engagement across Europe.

In his later years, Vadian was known for his advocacy of tolerance and his defense of the rights of minority groups.

As he once said, 'A free people is a happy people.'

This phrase encapsulates the essence of Vadian's commitment to liberty and democracy, leaving a lasting impact on the world of politics and philosophy.
